description: Golden briefs for npm run eval:formats: one short sample per format, rendered and scored against the format's cadence target (kit/core/cadence.mjs CADENCE_TARGETS) and the scorecard's metric targets (eval/scorecard.mjs). A sample is an example project (dir), a window of the long-form beat-map fixture (beat-map), or a Short cut from it (short).

briefs.label: Short form
briefs.brief: A 9:16 Short cut from the long-form explainer: opens on a number or a piece of evidence, never a title card; a visual event every 2–3 s; word captions on; loops back to the hook.

briefs.label: Talking-head base edit
briefs.brief: A presenter recording, trimmed, with graphics dressed beside the face and full-frame inserts for the numbers; the face holds the personal lines.

briefs.label: Full art direction
briefs.brief: A narrated product story with a designed world: brand palette and type on every frame, cinematic transitions, a hero shot per beat.

briefs.label: Long-form explainer
briefs.brief: One minute of the 16-minute explainer's direction map: builds of 2–4 states over a chapter plate, a hard cut every 15–25 s, every claim on a sourced visual.

briefs.label: Motion graphics
briefs.brief: A short design-led promo where motion is the message: kinetic type, a stat hit, a process, a logo row, a call to action.

briefs.label: Animated short and long form
briefs.brief: A character-led story: cast acting the key action of each beat in a set, with narration and captions.

animation.description: The six animation briefs of docs/ANIMATION_PIPELINE_RFC.md §8.3 for npm run eval:formats -- --animation. Each is a 30–45 second 9:16 character Short, run once through launchclip make --animation and once through the create-video skill, then scored from the finished project (eval/animation-metrics.mjs). brief is the prompt both paths are given, word for word. exercises says what the brief is there to stress. expect holds the checks only this brief has. stand_in, where a brief has one, is a hand-authored example scored when no run is given, to show the scorecard working; it is never used for a path's run and never enters the parity table.

briefs.label: A problem and a fix
briefs.brief: A 35-second vertical animated Short with two characters. A cafe owner keeps losing orders she writes on sticky notes; her friend shows her a shared order board on a tablet; she tries it and the next rush goes smoothly. Play it as a scene between the two of them, not as an advert read by a narrator.
exercises: two characters who both speak and both act
the problem landing inside the profile's limit
a product shown through what a character does with it, not through narration
the whole chain of contracts on the plainest case

briefs.label: POV
briefs.brief: POV: you typed "quick question" in the team chat and now six people are typing. A 30-second vertical animated Short with one character caught in that moment.
exercises: the pov skeleton chosen from the brief
one character carrying the whole video on face and pose
the second person address: the viewer is the character
a cast of one through the bible and the shot list

briefs.label: The last time
briefs.brief: The last time your dad walked you to the bus stop. A 35-second vertical animated Short: a parent and a child on an ordinary morning, then the same two people years later.
exercises: the last-time skeleton chosen from the brief
two characters in an ordinary moment with no problem to solve by talking
the skeleton's key shot and what the rig can and cannot perform
a quiet register: few lines, slow delivery

briefs.label: An argument
briefs.brief: A 40-second vertical animated Short. Two flatmates argue about whether plates need rinsing before they go in the dishwasher. It is almost all dialogue, each of them sure they are right, and by the end one of them is shown to be wrong.
exercises: dense dialogue: speaker turns per minute at the top of the band
the speaker on screen on every line, with reactions from the listener
the longest stretch on one framing when two people stand and talk
lip sync under fast back-and-forth

briefs.label: A silent story
briefs.brief: A 30-second vertical animated Short with almost no dialogue. One character tries to put together a flat-pack chair without reading the instructions while a second character watches. Tell it through what they do and how they look; at most two lines are spoken.
exercises: silent lines and their lengths in the script contract
acting carrying the story: poses, expressions and actions per minute
captions, the mix and the lip-sync gate with almost no speech
a character who acts and never speaks still counting as used

briefs.label: Three characters, one nearly silent
briefs.brief: A 40-second vertical animated Short with three characters. Two colleagues plan a surprise party in loud whispers across a desk; the third, who the party is for, sits between them wearing headphones and says one line at the very end.
exercises: three characters kept apart: three voices, three designs, each with its own must_keep
staging three people in 9:16 without anyone leaving the safe area
a character who barely speaks staying present through reactions
every listed character speaking or acting
